notes.prompting: Closed book, single turn, no tools. Azure OpenAI Responses API with instructions 'Answer from memory. Be concise; give only the answer.' and max_output_tokens=4000 (retried at 16000 if a reasoning model returned no text).
notes.accuracy: Errors / empty responses count as incorrect; n is the full item count.
notes.event_year: Exact year; within_1 = |pred-gold| <= 1. Prediction = first 3-4 digit integer.
notes.number_one: Normalized title match (accents, case, punctuation, parentheticals ignored); artist not required.
notes.leader: Name matcher: last significant token, or two significant tokens, or regnal name + numeral; accent-folded with a small given-name exonym table.
notes.cpi: First number in the response (excluding the two years and 100), within 3% of 100*CPI[Y2]/CPI[Y1].
notes.leader_unambiguity: Leader items are unambiguous within slashyear's checked leader record: exactly one holder of the title is recorded for that state and year, with a tenure spanning the whole year. A year where a second holder was dropped by slashyear's cross-check could still show one recorded holder.
notes.leader_matcher_check: Manual read of 30 randomly sampled graded leader items (all 3 models, seed 7): 30/30 grades agreed with a human reading. All leader items graded wrong were also read (11 across the 3 models): 4 are matcher false negatives (Roshdy/Rushdi transliteration x3, 'Mahmud Bey' for Mahmud ibn Muhammad x1), 3 are a numbering convention in the gold (gold 'Francis II' [HRE numbering], models said 'Francis I of Austria', same person), 4 are genuine errors. Leader accuracy is therefore understated by up to ~1-1.2 points per model.
notes.errors: 2 items (ev-0078, ev-0367) were rejected by the Azure content filter (HTTP 400) for all three models; they count as wrong. No other API errors after retries.
